name: Magento
title: Magento SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on Magento Open Source: 26 of 43 services wired, with cart, checkout and sign-in; reviews and wishlist are not. Setup, settings and limits.
lede: Customer sign-in through Magento’s `/V1/integration/customer/token` works well, and cart, checkout and sign-in are all wired. Reviews and wishlist are gaps because Magento ships no REST surface for either.
verdict: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; reviews and wishlist are not, because Magento has no REST API for them. The catch is the catalogue: it needs an admin or integration token, and the connector takes that token from a `PUBLIC_` variable, which the browser receives.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your Magento store

env.name: PUBLIC_MAGENTO_API_URL
env.note: Your Magento base URL; the connector builds `{url}/rest[/{store_code}]/V1`. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_MAGENTO_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.note: An admin or integration access token. The connector sends it on catalogue, CMS, order, coupon and store-configuration calls, which reject a customer token. See the limitations.

env.name: PUBLIC_MAGENTO_STORE_ID
env.note: A store view code, such as `default`, used to scope requests. Used only when it looks like a code rather than a numeric ID.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/magento-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_MAGENTO_*` variable that is set, camel-cased. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_MAGENTO_API_KEY`, `PUBLIC_MAGENTO_API_SECRET`, `PUBLIC_MAGENTO_ACCESS_KEY` and `PUBLIC_MAGENTO_CHANNEL_ID`; the connector’s source does not read them.
backendSettings: Since Magento 2.4.4, an integration token works as a standalone bearer token only once you enable Stores › Configuration › Services › OAuth › Consumer Settings › “Allow OAuth Access Tokens to be used as standalone Bearer tokens” (`bin/magento config:set oauth/consumer/enable_integration_as_bearer 1`). Without it, every admin route returns 401.
howItWorks: The connector speaks Magento’s REST API under `/rest/V1`, scoped to a store view when one is set. It picks a token per call: the shopper’s customer token for their own cart and account, the admin or integration token for catalogue, CMS, orders and coupons — which have no shopper-level access — and no token at all for guest carts and search.
limitations: Reviews: not wired — `Magento_Review` ships no `webapi.xml`, so there is no REST surface to call.
Wishlist: not wired — `Magento_Wishlist` ships no `webapi.xml` either.

The admin or integration token the connector needs for the catalogue comes from `PUBLIC_MAGENTO_ACCESS_TOKEN`. SvelteKit sends `PUBLIC_` variables to the browser, so every visitor to the store can read that token and use whatever access the integration has.

troubleshooting.fix: On Magento 2.4.4 and later, enable “Allow OAuth Access Tokens to be used as standalone Bearer tokens” (`bin/magento config:set oauth/consumer/enable_integration_as_bearer 1`). Until you do, an integration token is refused on every admin route.

faq.q: Can I run a Magento store on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; reviews and wishlist are not. The obstacle is the catalogue token: the connector needs an admin or integration token and reads it from a `PUBLIC_` variable, which every visitor’s browser receives. Weigh that before deploying.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to Magento?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/magento-connector`, set `PUBLIC_MAGENTO_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: Why are reviews and wishlists missing on Magento?
faq.a: Because Magento has no REST API for them: the `Magento_Review` and `Magento_Wishlist` modules ship no `webapi.xml`. The Svelte Commerce maintainers have asked Magento’s maintainers whether exposing them is planned, or whether a custom module is the expected answer.

openQuestion: Is exposing a REST surface for reviews and wishlist planned, or is a custom module the expected answer?

api.surface: The connector calls Magento’s REST Web API at `{url}/rest[/{store_code}]/V1`, a single JSON namespace scoped to a store view code when one is set.
api.auth: Every call carries `Authorization: Bearer` with a token chosen per route: the admin or integration token for catalogue, orders and CMS, the shopper’s customer token from `POST /V1/integration/customer/token` (kept in `localStorage` as `customer_token`) for `/V1/customers/me` and `/V1/carts/mine`, and no header at all for guest carts, search and the token endpoints.

calls.what: `GET /V1/products` with `searchCriteria[filter_groups]`, `searchCriteria[sortOrders]`, `searchCriteria[pageSize]` and `searchCriteria[currentPage]`; `GET /V1/products/{sku}` for one product and `GET /V1/configurable-products/{sku}/children` for its variants
`GET /V1/categories/list` filtered on `is_active` and `level`, or on `url_key` to resolve a slug; `GET /V1/categories/{id}` for one category
`GET /V1/search` with `search_term` and `searchCriteria[requestName]`, then `GET /V1/products` filtered on `entity_id in` the returned IDs
`POST /V1/guest-carts` or `POST /V1/carts/mine` to create the cart, then `GET`, `GET /totals`, `POST /items`, `PUT` and `DELETE /items/{itemId}` under the same prefix
`POST {cart}/shipping-information`, `GET {cart}/payment-methods` to resolve a method code, then `POST {cart}/payment-information` to place the order
`GET /V1/orders` with `searchCriteria` filters on `customer_id`, `customer_email`, `status` or `increment_id`, and `GET /V1/orders/{id}`, both with the admin token
`GET /V1/customers/me`, then `PUT /V1/customers/me` with the whole customer and its edited `addresses` array

rules: List routes need `searchCriteria`, so `searchCriteria[currentPage]` is always sent; filters inside one group are joined with OR and groups with AND, and the totals are read from `total_count` in the body, because Magento sends no pagination headers.

Every cart route exists twice, under `/V1/guest-carts/{maskedId}` with no token and under `/V1/carts/mine` with the customer token, and the connector picks the pair per session; `POST /V1/guest-carts` answers with the masked cart ID as a bare JSON string.
The quote carries no totals, so each cart read is two calls, `GET {cart}` and `GET {cart}/totals`.

The store view code must be set for carts, because a cart created through the unscoped `/rest/V1/guest-carts` gets `store_id` 0 and then rejects valid coupons; a numeric store ID is ignored rather than placed in the path.

`url_key`, descriptions, images, `special_price` and the `meta_*` fields are read from the product’s `custom_attributes` array, not from top-level fields, and since Magento has no `PATCH`, updates are a read followed by a full `PUT`.
